elements.label: Figure 1.1
elements.description:
Line chart with two y-axes and a shared year x-axis (1993–2020). Left y-axis: "Poverty rate (%)", 0–100 in steps of 10. Right y-axis: "GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$)", 0–3,000 in steps of 500. X-axis labels run every year from 1993 to 2020. No data values are printed on the chart, so values are approximate readings.

Legend (two rows):
- Extreme poverty ($1.90/day 2011PPP), teal line, left axis
- LMIC PL ($3.20/day 2011PPP), orange line, left axis
- UMIC PL ($5.50/day 2011PPP), grey line, left axis
- GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$), yellow line, right axis

Approximate readings by series (poverty series plotted at 1993, 1998, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2008, then 2010–2020 in two-year steps):
- Extreme poverty: 1993 ~52, 1998 ~31, 2002 ~37, 2004 ~26, 2006 ~19, 2008 ~14; 2010 ~4, 2012 ~2.5, 2014 ~2.5, 2016 ~2, 2018 ~2, 2020 ~1
- LMIC PL: 1993 ~80, 1998 ~69, 2002 ~70, 2004 ~60, 2006 ~50, 2008 ~46; 2010 ~17, 2012 ~13, 2014 ~11, 2016 ~8, 2018 ~7, 2020 ~5
- UMIC PL: 1993 ~95, 1998 ~90, 2002 ~89, 2004 ~84, 2006 ~80, 2008 ~77; 2010 ~47, 2012 ~41, 2014 ~35, 2016 ~27, 2018 ~23, 2020 ~19
- GDP per capita (right axis): 1993 ~460, 1998 ~670, 2002 ~900, 2008 ~1,280, 2010 ~1,400, 2012 ~1,560, 2014 ~1,740, 2016 ~1,910, 2018 ~2,230, 2019 ~2,450, 2020 ~2,600

Note printed below the chart: "Poverty measurement methodology changed in 2010, rendering a break in series comparability." Source: World Bank WDI, PovcalNet.

Pattern: all three poverty rates fall over time, with a visible break at 2010 where the series restart at lower levels. GDP per capita rises steadily and steeply across the whole period.
